cat > /workspace/submission/README.md <<'EOF'
# Offline QUIC receive / canonical-wire audit

`src/offline/Main` reads the normalised metadata produced by the public metadata adapter
(`/workspace/format_io.py`) and prints exactly one JSON result.

    python3 /workspace/build.py /workspace/submission/src /workspace/tmp/classes
    python3 /workspace/run.py /workspace/tmp/classes < input.json

## Layout

| file | purpose |
|---|---|
| `offline/Main.java` | format-only adapter (unchanged): reads the normalised trace lines, prints the JSON result |
| `offline/ReceiveAudit.java` | the receive audit: envelope framing, packet number reconstruction, routing, authentication, key epochs, frame transaction, canonical envelopes and the result snapshot |
| `offline/QuicVarint.java` | QUIC unsigned varint helpers (minimal encoding, tolerant decoding) |
| `offline/Frame.java` | decoded frame plus its canonical (minimal varint) encoding |
| `offline/FrameError.java` | semantic/encoding failure of a frame, carries the payload offset |
| `offline/ByteStore.java` | sparse byte storage for stream payloads and CRYPTO data |
| `offline/IntervalSet.java` | merged, disjoint, half open interval set (ACK ranges, retired sequences) |
| `offline/Journal.java` | undo log of one packet transaction |

The retained TLS-Attacker codec was repaired where it was unfinished for this contract:

* `VariableLengthIntegerEncoding` reports the minimal width, decodes with the consumed width and
  can check whether an encoding is minimal; the stream reader rejects truncated integers.
* `AckFrame` keeps all additional ack ranges; `AckFrameParser` parses them and
  `AckFrameSerializer` writes them again.
* `StreamFrameSerializer` derives the optional offset/length fields from the frame type instead of
  from nullable DTO fields, so lengthless frames stay lengthless.

## Semantics

* Envelopes are framed per datagram; a malformed header records one `BAD_HEADER` attempt and
  abandons the remainder of that datagram without touching the connection state.
* Packet numbers are reconstructed as the non negative number congruent to the truncated value
  that is closest to the expected number (ties choose the larger one).
* Every packet is processed as one transaction: the first frame error rolls back streams, bytes,
  credits, ACK/ECN state, both connection id registries, retirement thresholds and key epochs,
  closes the connection and keeps the previously committed packets.
* Accepted packets are normalised: the payload is re-encoded with minimal varints, the header keeps
  level, connection ids, token and key phase, and the packet number uses the smallest width that
  reconstructs the same number.
EOF
